context: A teacher walks a teen through historical research
purpose: Teach: 名付け/生体/養護/反乱/母国/生き残っ/操縦/発酵

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 桜さん、研究、地名に名付けられた歴史、深く論じていますね。
lines.en: Sakura, your research on the history of place names is quite deeply argued.
lines.style: Warm, observant tone. Measured pace. Slight lean forward—genuine recognition of the student's work. Approachable authority, not distancing.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい。生体への被害、戦争時、深刻でした。
lines.en: Yes. The biological damage during wartime was severe.
lines.style: Steady, serious commitment. Eyes held. Speaking from something read and felt, not performed. Small breath before 'severe'—weight on it.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 当時の養護院、戦災孤児を、受け入れていましたね。
lines.en: Care facilities at the time—they were accepting war orphans, weren't they.
lines.style: Gentle reflective tone, almost conversational. Not lecturing. Trailing upward slightly on the end—genuinely asking her to confirm, to remember with her.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい。民衆の反乱、歴史の節目に、何度かありました。
lines.en: Yes. There were several moments in history when the common people rose up in revolt.
lines.style: Clear and direct. Speaking from careful research. Slightly faster on the factual content, then a small pause. Not defensive—assured in what she's learned.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 戦後、母国に帰れなかった人々、忘れてはなりませんね。
lines.en: We must not forget the people who couldn't return to their home countries after the war.
lines.style: Quiet gravity. Slower pace on 'must not forget'—these words matter. Looking at her, not past her. The tone of someone speaking something true.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい。戦災を生き残った市民、その声、論文で拾いました。
lines.en: Yes. I included the voices of the civilians who survived the war in my paper.
lines.style: Modest confidence. Speaking factually about her own work. Slight warmth underneath—she knows she did something right. Even pace, no rushing.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 政治の操縦、誰の手にあったか、論じていますね。
lines.en: You've discussed whose hands controlled the political narrative, haven't you.
lines.style: Engaged, real interest in the answer. Leaning slightly into the question. Tone of someone wanting to understand her thinking, not testing her.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい。発酵食文化、戦時下でも、人々を支えました。
lines.en: Yes. Fermented food culture sustained people even during wartime.
lines.style: Thoughtful connection, almost discovering it as she speaks. Softer ending—this detail feels tender to her. Small fade on the final word, like opening a door to something human.
